items.title: Reject Java constants that exceed the constant-pool slots (R3.12)
items.head: e0dbc3a5b60b140f26f3622f34c11035e3c1cb7d
items.problem: A Long or Double in the final declared pool slot was accepted without its required second slot. At constant_pool_count = 65535 the u16 cursor overflowed while advancing past that entry.
items.change: Check the next pool index before retaining each constant. Reject a wide entry whose reserved slot does not fit, while preserving correctly formed maximum-size pools.
items.coverage: Long and Double entries at ordinary and maximum u16 boundaries, valid two-slot tail entries, ordinary constants and an existing class fixture.
items.deduplication: Earlier Java work covered bytecode-wide opcodes and method descriptors; this change validates constant-pool slot accounting.
items.body:
## Roadmap

R3.12: Reject Java Long and Double constants without their reserved constant-pool slot, including the maximum u16 pool boundary.

## Problem

A Long or Double in the final declared pool slot was accepted without its required second slot. At constant_pool_count = 65535 the u16 cursor overflowed while advancing past that entry.

## Change

Check the next pool index before retaining each constant. Reject a wide entry whose reserved slot does not fit, while preserving correctly formed maximum-size pools.

## Verification

4 new integration tests cover long and Double entries at ordinary and maximum u16 boundaries, valid two-slot tail entries, ordinary constants and an existing class fixture. The fixtures use synthetic bytes.

The exact source head passed 957 formats-crate tests, `cargo fmt --all --check` and formats-crate Clippy with warnings denied: https://github.com/Afloat16/claude-mem/actions/runs/42633003467/job/129213811541

## Related work

Earlier Java work covered bytecode-wide opcodes and method descriptors; this change validates constant-pool slot accounting.

items.title: Keep embedded Godot pack reads before the trailer (R3.12)
items.head: 9744a0569a7c51d8938ce645e52f9a66965fb1e2
items.problem: The embedded PCK directory and member reader used the executable's complete length as the pack boundary. This let damaged entries consume the twelve-byte embedded-pack trailer as table fields or member data.
items.change: Exclude the embedded trailer from directory parsing and stored-member reads, mark members crossing that boundary unreadable, and enforce it when an entry is passed directly to the reader.
items.coverage: PCK versions 1, 2 and 3; member ranges in the footer, directory counts and records crossing it, direct reads of forged entries, and valid embedded/standalone packs.
items.deduplication: Earlier Godot contributions covered installation and process paths; this change bounds the embedded PCK parser and extractor.
items.body:
## Roadmap

R3.12: Keep embedded Godot pack tables and member reads before the executable's pack trailer.

## Problem

The embedded PCK directory and member reader used the executable's complete length as the pack boundary. This let damaged entries consume the twelve-byte embedded-pack trailer as table fields or member data.

## Change

Exclude the embedded trailer from directory parsing and stored-member reads, mark members crossing that boundary unreadable, and enforce it when an entry is passed directly to the reader.

## Verification

4 new integration tests cover pCK versions 1, 2 and 3; member ranges in the footer, directory counts and records crossing it, direct reads of forged entries, and valid embedded/standalone packs. The fixtures use synthetic bytes.

## Related work

items.title: Bound retained metadata when listing Node SEA programs (R3.12)
items.head: b8f989a9ab8627c95c01f8337a8d8fd3d9a95bd0
items.problem: SEA parsing retained every declared asset and argument before applying the output entry cap. Argument strings and asset keys could also expand without a shared decoded text budget.
items.change: Retain only the bounded asset/argument inventory and at most 8 MiB of decoded metadata text, including replacement-character expansion. Omit oversized fields whole, preserve declared totals, mark truncation, and continue validating every skipped binary field.
items.coverage: Entry limits including empty arguments, oversized paths/keys, invalid UTF-8 expansion, malformed bytes after the retained prefix and ordinary metadata.
items.deduplication: No matching Node SEA retained-inventory or decoded-text budget change appeared in the checked histories.
items.body:

R3.12: Bound retained Node SEA asset and argument metadata while still validating the complete blob layout.

items.title: Respect the UTF-8 output budget for IL2CPP literals (R3.12)
items.head: d81b7d5705461ef4425c33a03de4252f5f096f13
items.problem: Literal extraction limited input bytes, then used lossy UTF-8 conversion. Replacement characters could make the returned string larger than the advertised maximum, and a cut multi-byte character could be reported as damaged text.
items.change: Build literal text within the output byte budget, preserve Unicode boundaries and charge the full replacement-character width. Keep the completeness flag tied to consumed original bytes.
items.coverage: ASCII and empty values, multi-byte UTF-8 across every short boundary, invalid bytes, incomplete input sequences and replacement expansion.
items.deduplication: The existing IL2CPP owner checks validate declaring types. This change bounds literal text output.
items.body:
## Roadmap

R3.12: Keep shortened IL2CPP literals within their UTF-8 output budget without inventing a partial character.

## Problem

Literal extraction limited input bytes, then used lossy UTF-8 conversion. Replacement characters could make the returned string larger than the advertised maximum, and a cut multi-byte character could be reported as damaged text.

## Change

Build literal text within the output byte budget, preserve Unicode boundaries and charge the full replacement-character width. Keep the completeness flag tied to consumed original bytes.

## Verification

4 new integration tests cover aSCII and empty values, multi-byte UTF-8 across every short boundary, invalid bytes, incomplete input sequences and replacement expansion. The fixtures use synthetic bytes.

items.title: Decode Unity R16 and RG16 textures (R3.9)

items.title: Preserve DEX boundaries when member or handler lists are capped (R3.12)
items.head: 149f060b9959e8906327e799088728820659513c
items.problem: A capped class-data group left its unread records at the cursor, then interpreted them as the following group. Capped or incomplete typed-handler lists could likewise turn their remaining bytes into a fabricated catch-all address.
items.change: Return retained class members as incomplete before crossing an unconsumed group, and read a catch-all only after every declared typed handler was decoded.
items.coverage: Over-cap and exact-cap class members; oversized, truncated, empty and exact-cap typed-handler lists with real catch-all controls.
items.deduplication: Earlier DEX work covered LEB values, MUTF-8, register lists and array widths. This change preserves record alignment when retention limits are reached.
items.body:
## Roadmap

R3.12: Stop capped DEX member and handler lists from interpreting unread records as the following field or a catch-all.

## Problem

A capped class-data group left its unread records at the cursor, then interpreted them as the following group. Capped or incomplete typed-handler lists could likewise turn their remaining bytes into a fabricated catch-all address.

## Change

Return retained class members as incomplete before crossing an unconsumed group, and read a catch-all only after every declared typed handler was decoded.

## Verification

5 new integration tests cover over-cap and exact-cap class members; oversized, truncated, empty and exact-cap typed-handler lists with real catch-all controls. The fixtures use synthetic bytes.

items.title: Keep Android resource children inside their parent chunks (R3.12)
items.head: ea680eeb9e9267e54e304448596fd947cc18f3d5
items.problem: A resource child could fit the physical input while crossing the size declared by its enclosing table or package. String-pool offsets, library records and short child headers could therefore borrow unrelated bytes.
items.change: Bound each reader to its declared parent, require complete package/known-child headers, keep package string pools inside the package payload, and retain only complete fixed-width library records.
items.coverage: Table/package crossings, escaped package pools, retained earlier entries, sibling library data, short headers, truncated bag parents and both legacy 284-byte and current 288-byte package headers.
items.deduplication: PR #698 bounded a string pool by its own chunk. This change enforces the enclosing table/package and sibling-child boundaries; it does not replace that pool implementation.
items.body:
## Roadmap

R3.12: Keep Android resource packages, child chunks and library records inside their enclosing declared ranges.

## Problem

A resource child could fit the physical input while crossing the size declared by its enclosing table or package. String-pool offsets, library records and short child headers could therefore borrow unrelated bytes.

## Change

Bound each reader to its declared parent, require complete package/known-child headers, keep package string pools inside the package payload, and retain only complete fixed-width library records.

## Verification

7 new integration tests cover table/package crossings, escaped package pools, retained earlier entries, sibling library data, short headers, truncated bag parents and both legacy 284-byte and current 288-byte package headers. The fixtures use synthetic bytes.

Verification of the current source head is in progress; no passing CI result is claimed yet.

## Related work

PR #698 bounded a string pool by its own chunk. This change enforces the enclosing table/package and sibling-child boundaries; it does not replace that pool implementation.

items.title: Bound WebAssembly metadata across repeated custom sections (R3.12)
items.head: 6425e7b64a8e95f1b5b14632835442bd024b8855
items.problem: Every repeated name or producers custom section received a new allowance. Their combined retained inventories could exceed MAX_ITEMS, and the existing local cutoffs silently omitted metadata without setting the report's truncation flag.
items.change: Share the function-name, producer-field and producer-value limits across the entire module. Permit updates to retained function names at the cap and report both local and global omissions.
items.coverage: Repeated function-name sections, updates at the cap, producer values and empty fields across sections, each local cutoff and an ordinary module fixture.
items.deduplication: PR #1126 validates custom debug/source-map strings. This change bounds retained name and producer inventories across repeated sections.
items.body:
## Roadmap

R3.12: Apply WebAssembly name and producer inventory limits across repeated custom sections and report truncation.

## Problem

Every repeated name or producers custom section received a new allowance. Their combined retained inventories could exceed MAX_ITEMS, and the existing local cutoffs silently omitted metadata without setting the report's truncation flag.

## Change

Share the function-name, producer-field and producer-value limits across the entire module. Permit updates to retained function names at the cap and report both local and global omissions.

## Verification

5 new integration tests cover repeated function-name sections, updates at the cap, producer values and empty fields across sections, each local cutoff and an ordinary module fixture. The fixtures use synthetic bytes.

Verification of the current source head is in progress; no passing CI result is claimed yet.

## Related work

items.title: Validate Unity serialized metadata ranges before reading (R3.12)
items.head: de9d7444f5098a3e6c27b32f3b5249d4bb2743fc
items.problem: The metadata reader accepted a header offset beyond a short input and read past the declared metadata region into object bytes. The string reader could panic on an impossible starting offset.
items.change: Validate metadata offset and size with checked arithmetic against the object-data boundary, declared file length and available input. Parse only the resulting metadata slice.
items.coverage: Every prefix before the metadata end, shortened declared metadata, arithmetic overflow and impossible public Header ranges, plus equality of full-file and exact-prefix results.
items.deduplication: PR #890 validates serialized object extents. This change validates the separate metadata header and reader range.
items.body:
## Roadmap

R3.12: Validate Unity serialized metadata offsets and lengths before reading so short inputs cannot panic or borrow object bytes.

## Problem

The metadata reader accepted a header offset beyond a short input and read past the declared metadata region into object bytes. The string reader could panic on an impossible starting offset.

## Change

Validate metadata offset and size with checked arithmetic against the object-data boundary, declared file length and available input. Parse only the resulting metadata slice.

## Verification

4 new integration tests cover every prefix before the metadata end, shortened declared metadata, arithmetic overflow and impossible public Header ranges, plus equality of full-file and exact-prefix results. The fixtures use synthetic bytes.

items.title: Decode Unreal floating-point texture formats (R3.9)
items.head: 75b507c0b96fe22c8f8a1e517c31ef6cee207a01
items.problem: Cooked Unreal textures with supported half- and full-precision channel layouts were reported as unsupported because their pixel-format names were not mapped to the shared float decoder.
items.change: Route scalar, red/green and RGBA half/full precision formats, including the filtered half aliases, through the bounded pixel reader. RGB converts from linear values to 8-bit sRGB; alpha stays linear and values are clipped for PNG output.
items.coverage: Cooked package fixtures reaching all six channel layouts, filtered aliases, negative/non-finite values, alpha behavior, stored row order, short mips, zero/huge dimensions and output budgets.
items.deduplication: The existing float decoder was connected to Unity formats. This adds Unreal format dispatch and cooked-package regression coverage.
items.body:
## Roadmap

R3.9: Unreal: decode cooked half- and full-precision floating-point textures with the shared bounded pixel reader.

## Problem

Cooked Unreal textures with supported half- and full-precision channel layouts were reported as unsupported because their pixel-format names were not mapped to the shared float decoder.

## Change

Route scalar, red/green and RGBA half/full precision formats, including the filtered half aliases, through the bounded pixel reader. RGB converts from linear values to 8-bit sRGB; alpha stays linear and values are clipped for PNG output.

## Verification

4 new integration tests cover cooked package fixtures reaching all six channel layouts, filtered aliases, negative/non-finite values, alpha behavior, stored row order, short mips, zero/huge dimensions and output budgets. The fixtures use synthetic bytes.

The previous source head `5b17be5ae2a00e9e93959793ed254335a8177d76` passed 957 formats-crate tests and Clippy. Its formatting difference has been corrected; verification of the current head is pending. Previous result: https://github.com/Afloat16/claude-mem/actions/runs/42633003467/job/129213811079

## Related work

The existing float decoder was connected to Unity formats. This adds Unreal format dispatch and cooked-package regression coverage.
